explanation: There is no basis for treating the head as 'the seat of the soul' in Islamic teaching — in fact, a well-known hadith encourages gently stroking an orphan's head as an act of kindness, so the gesture toward children is generally read as affectionate rather than offensive. Toward an adult, especially an elder or someone you don't know well, patting the head comes across as condescending or overly familiar rather than a religious violation.
local_tip: Reserve head-patting for children you know, and use a handshake or a warm word instead with adults.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, so touching anyone's head, child or adult, is a serious breach of etiquette.
Patting a child's head is often affectionate, but touching an adult's head, especially by a stranger, reads as condescending.
Patting a child's head is usually read as friendly, though doing it to an adult can still seem patronizing.

sources.title: Hadith on Orphans: Be kind to orphans for a soft heart
